newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures mixed in a trade lull before FOMC.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures mixed in a trade lull before FOMC.

text.p: U.S. debt futures traded narrowly mixed early after pricing in a 25-basis-point U.S. interest rate hike last week, traders and floor analysts said.
"After last Thursday's Greenspan comments the market priced in a rate hike," one Eurodollar futures floor trader said. "It's a foregone conclusion."
In testimony to Congress on Thursday, U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan laid the groundwork for a pre-emptive rate hike, citing strong demand in the U.S. labor sector.
A bond broker said any accompanying text to a Federal Open Market Committee announcement on rates will be scrutinized.
"If the text indicates it was a pre-emptive hike, I think the market will do alright," he said.

Several traders said the tone in U.S. bonds was soft but not heavy, as the long-end continued to outperform the short-end. June T-bonds rose to 108-27/32, above resistance at 108-23/32 to 108-24/32. The yield curve immediately flattened following Greenspan's comments late last week.
Soon after the opening of Monday's pit session, one U.S. firm sold 4,000 two-year note futures.
"It was a flattener," one bond futures trader said, but cited little activity in the bond pit.

Most traders believe U.S. debt futures will rally if the FOMC decides to raise short-term rates by 25 basis points on Tuesday. Resistance is at 109-09/32 for June bonds and 93.89 for September Eurodollars.
"Most are hoping for a rally in which to sell into," one bond trader said, noting the last week's active curve flattening trades of buying bonds and selling notes.
However, a rally in bonds could be muted by the U.S. Treasury department's $17.25 billion two-year note auction, which will also be held on Tuesday, March 25.
"If the results of the two-year note auction are strong it will be because of short-covering," one trader said.
He added that note short-covering could force some traders and dealers to liquidate long bond positions.
On Wednesday, March 26, the U.S. Treasury department will sell $12.5 billion five-year notes and $13.75 billion one-year notes.
In addition, some traders are looking for another Fed rate hike later in the year, which would keep the downtrend in Eurodollars and bonds intact.
"I don't see a bullish scenario," a Eurodollar trader said.
He expects September Eurodollars to eventually test support at 93.75 and 93.69, and said a drop to 93.60 would be "fairly prices for another round of hikes."
At 0846 CST/1446 GMT, June T-bonds were up 03/32 at 108-26/32, 10-year notes were off 02/32 at 106-13/32, and September Eurodollars were up 0.005 at 93.815.
